A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMPEL research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison: v1 contains Appendices A–B, while v2 contains expanded Appendices A–B and a new Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO policy evaluations, ablations, computational measurements, and appendix learning curves.

after.justification: v2 retains original LIBERO experiments and adds pruning, routing, sensitivity, longer-sequence, and trajectory-analysis results.

M1.justification: v2 implements pruning of underactivated experts every ten tasks in the 30-task experiment (Appendix B.1); v1 only suggested pruning as a possibility. This is a limited procedural extension. The base architecture, dynamic expert fusion, orthogonal initialization, and coefficient replay remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use LIBERO-90 for pretraining and the same Goal, Spatial, Object, and Long manipulation tasks (Table 3). The 30-task study concatenates already evaluated Object, Goal, and Spatial tasks; sequence length, ordering, and demonstration-count variations change the protocol within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding main comparisons retain SeqFT variants, ER, EWC, PackNet, LOTUS, TAIL, L2M, IsCiL, and multitask references (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 3). New analyses reuse existing comparators; the added routing variants are ablations.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols covering three task orders, ranks 2–32, demonstration counts 1–50, Sigmoid versus Softmax routing, pruning thresholds, and a concatenated 30-task sequence with periodic pruning. These substantially expand experimental controls and testing procedures. The original ten-epoch training and evaluation-every-two-epochs schedule remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds pruning tests, representation-drift visualization, task-order/rank/data sensitivity, router-activation comparisons, 30-task scalability analysis, and trajectory case studies. Figure 5 also adds a layer-wise coefficient ablation while removing v1's random-initialization and output-merging ablations. The diagnostic evidence changes substantially.

E5.justification: Both Appendix A.2 sections specify seeds 100, 200, and 300 and reporting means and standard deviations over three runs. v2 introduces no new repeated-run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test.

E6.justification: New pruning, representation, sensitivity, 30-task, and trajectory findings substantially expand the results (v2 Figures 6b and 7–13). Existing Figure 5 values also change: Goal AUC for top-1 experts changes from 69 to 68, and for all experts from 75 to 76; the default remains 78. Most main benchmark values and rankings are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (6) corrects multiplication order from W0x and the low-rank product times x to xW0 and x times the low-rank product, consistent with the stated input-by-output matrix dimensions. This is a limited dimensional correction. The formal problem, objectives, metrics, and replay loss otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that dynamically combining a progressive expert library improves forward transfer and that coefficient replay limits forgetting with low parameter, storage, and computational costs. The principal LIBERO superiority claims retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations contrasting independent Sigmoid coefficients with competing Softmax weights, and identifies limited router capacity as a possible explanation for declining 30-task performance. It discusses router expansion and alternative logit replay as future directions. These extend the existing mechanism discussion and applicability limitations.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 substantially expand training and inference documentation. v2 also discloses coefficient zero-padding as the library grows and FP32 router computation within otherwise FP16 execution. The repository link already existed in v1. The added ER description specifies 32 old plus 32 new samples but conflicts with the retained total-batch-size statement of 32.

R1.justification: v2 adds SKILL (Ge et al., 2024) and trims peripheral references and examples, including Gato, Octo, SAM, and image-generation LoRA merging. Positioning relative to TAIL, L2M, IsCiL, and model fusion remains largely unchanged. Publication-year and venue updates represent retained works.

P1.justification: v2 reformulates the introduction's contributions, condenses related work, moves detailed baseline descriptions to Appendix A.1, and combines the conclusion and limitations. It adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements. The overall main-section sequence and much method and results prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and relocates the method overview, expands the coefficient figure with a pruning panel, and adds numerous diagnostic plots and two algorithm displays. Tables are reformatted and learning-curve figures are redistributed and renumbered from Figures 7–10 to 14–17. This substantially changes visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 tests v1's pruning suggestion, adds useful robustness and scalability evidence, and makes implementation easier to audit through pseudocode and router details. The longer-sequence study also exposes an important capacity limitation. These support a modest net improvement, despite removal of two earlier ablations and the inconsistent new ER batch-size description; the central method and benchmark conclusions remain largely unchanged.
